stories.title: The market just wiped $500 billion off Google for spending on AI. Next up: Anthropic, losing $80.7 billion in six months, asking $1.5 to 2 trillion
stories.label: HOT
stories.window: Now to about 20 Nov. Listing expected mid-November (NBC, 26 Oct); the price range comes in an amended S-1, and that is the next turn. Best this week while E15 is still being pushed.
happening: Anthropic made its S-1 public on Mon 26 Oct: net loss $80.7 billion in the first six months of 2026 (against $42 billion for all of 2025); revenue up 1,368% year on year in the April-June quarter; about $141 billion raised and $112.4 billion in cash by June; listing expected mid-November on Nasdaq as ANT; Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley lead (NBC News, 26 Oct). NBC says the offering could value it at more than $2 trillion; Reuters and others say about $1.5 trillion. Use a range, or name who says it.

Its locked-in cloud commitments, as NBC lists them: Amazon at least $110 billion, SpaceX $120 billion, Google $115 billion, Microsoft $45 billion: $390 billion in total (NBC News, 26 Oct). Some reports say $430 billion; use NBC's $390 billion or skip.

The new turn: on Thu 29 Oct Alphabet fell 12.6%, its worst one-day drop ever, wiping about $500 billion (the second-biggest one-day wipeout in US history, after Nvidia's $589 billion in Jan 2025). Q3 revenue missed, and Alphabet's Philipp Schindler said search ad revenue underperformed partly because Google's own 'AI Mode' shows fewer ads. Alphabet has signed more than $1 trillion of multi-year AI spending agreements (NBC News, 29 Oct).

Already in Friday's email and still standing: OpenAI cut its own fundraising to about $20 billion at $1.25 trillion (from $30 billion at $1.4 trillion), per the FT via ThePrint and CoinDesk, 30-31 Oct.

No IPO price yet. Protos (27 Oct) derived about $71.43 a share from an S-1 footnote (a $2 billion charge settled with about 28 million shares), which implies about $1.2 trillion; it is a derived internal mark, not an IPO price. Use as colour only, if at all.
curiosity_gaps: Google's own AI just ate into Google's own ad business, and the market took $500 billion off it in one day. What happens when a company that only spends on AI asks for $1.5 trillion?
Anthropic lost more in six months ($80.7 billion) than it ever earned. Who buys that, the same month investors are dumping AI shares?
Our E15 viewers know the 'God share'. This is the next chapter: the timing, and whether the price holds.

stories.title: Binance lost $6.3 billion in about 20 minutes, the biggest crypto theft ever, and says its users won't pay a rupee. When WazirX lost about $230 million in 2024, Indian users did
stories.label: HOT
stories.window: About 3 to 5 days. Withdrawals resumed Sun 1 Nov; Binance planned a proof of reserves for Mon 2 Nov; the FBI named North Korea on Saturday. The next turns are the reserves report and how much of the remaining 10% is covered.
happening: On Thu 29 Oct, starting between 4:05 and 4:20 pm ET, about $6.3 billion moved out of Binance's hot wallets across 10 blockchains, most of it in about 20 minutes: about $3.8 billion in Ether and $1.5 billion in Bitcoin (18,270 BTC). It is the largest crypto theft on record, about four times Bybit's $1.5 billion in Feb 2025 (Wikipedia, citing CNBC and others; CNBC, 31 Oct).

How: Binance first pointed to a DevOps engineer's compromised laptop; co-CEO Richard Teng later said it was more complex than one engineer's permissions. The FBI on Saturday attributed it to North Korea's TraderTraitor group (Wikipedia; NPR, 31 Oct).

About $3 billion in stablecoins was frozen on-chain by Tether, Circle and Ripple; the $1.5 billion in Bitcoin could not be (Wikipedia, citing CNBC, 30 Oct). Bitcoin fell about 5%, below $80,000 (Wikipedia).

Binance: 'Binance will absorb the financial impact of these stolen funds, not our users.' By Saturday it said 90% of the stolen assets were covered (the top ten coins fully backed; the rest is less liquid tokens), using its SAFU user fund, part of its futures insurance fund and its corporate treasury. Withdrawals resumed on Sunday (CNBC, 31 Oct, updated 1 Nov). CNN puts coverage at about 95%.

The Indian contrast (context, older than a week): in July 2024 hackers took about $230 million from WazirX; its 16 million users had their accounts frozen and trading stayed shut for about 15 months, until a Singapore court approved a restructuring that does not repay them in full. Binance denied any responsibility for WazirX (Cointelegraph; Entrepreneur India).
curiosity_gaps: The world's biggest crypto exchange lost about ₹53,000 crore in 20 minutes and its users lost nothing. An Indian exchange lost a twenty-fifth of that and its users paid for it. What's the difference?
One engineer's laptop. That's where a $6.3 billion theft started, by Binance's own first account.
Your money on an exchange isn't in your wallet. Who pays when it's stolen depends on who you trusted.

facts.text: Started 29 Oct between 4:05 and 4:20 pm ET, about 20 minutes, 10 blockchains; about $6.3 bn ($6.3-6.4 bn); $3.8 bn Ether, $1.5 bn Bitcoin (18,270 BTC); about $3 bn frozen; Bitcoin -5% to below $80,000; TraderTraitor (North Korea); 'Binance will absorb the financial impact ..., not our users'; withdrawals resumed 1 Nov; proof of reserves planned 2 Nov.
facts.source: Wikipedia, '2026 Binance hack' (edited 2 Nov, citing CNBC, BBC, Guardian, NYT)

facts.text: About $6.3 bn stolen from hot wallets; 90% of stolen assets covered, top ten coins 100% backed, rest less liquid tokens; funded from SAFU, part of the futures insurance fund and the corporate treasury; withdrawals resumed Sunday; 90% covered does not mean 90% recovered from the attacker.
About 95% of the stolen amount covered; withdrawals resume.

Context: WazirX lost about $230 mn in July 2024; 16 mn users' accounts frozen; trading shut about 15 months until a Singapore court approved its restructuring; users not repaid in full. Binance: 'Binance has never operated WazirX.'

watch_out: No buy or sell call on any coin or exchange, and no 'move your crypto to X'. Facts and who paid only.
Coverage differs: 90% (Binance via CNBC, Saturday) vs about 95% (CNN, Sunday). Give the newer with the source, or say 'most of it'.

WazirX facts are 2024-25 context: check the latest repayment status before quoting a % (one review says 85%, low quality). 'Binance has never operated WazirX' is Binance's position; don't imply Binance owed WazirX users.
Rupee conversion: $6.3 bn is about ₹53,000 crore at about ₹84/$; others say ₹60,000 crore. Check the day's rate, or say $6.3 billion.
Crypto is a minority stake for our viewers; the line that travels is about trust (who pays), not about coins.
Bets: B1 stake in the first second; B3 a line worth sending inside 12 s; B4 split screen (Binance logo and $6.3 BILLION on top).

stories.lane: Deep lane (SEBI final order, 30 Oct; PTI via Daily Excelsior, 1 Nov; Bloomberg, 31 Oct)
stories.title: EKI Energy, the 2021 carbon-credit multibagger: SEBI says it pulled ₹197 crore of revenue forward and booked ₹26 crore of fictitious expenses. The fines on everyone add up to ₹88 lakh
stories.label: COLD
stories.window: About a week (to Sun 8 Nov). The next turns: an appeal to SAT, the recovery of the diverted ₹26 crore, or the stock's reaction on Monday. Credit SEBI's order in the caption.
happening: SEBI's 94-page final order (30 Oct) barred EKI Energy Services from the securities market for 2 months and its MD Manish Kumar Dabkara for 12 months; former CFO Mohit Kumar Agarwal 8 months; whole-time directors Naveen Sharma 5 months and Sonali Sheikh 1 month (PTI via Daily Excelsior, 1 Nov).

Findings: ₹197.04 crore of revenue recognised prematurely in the first three quarters of FY23, which SEBI called 'reckless financial misrepresentation connected with investor decisions concerning its listed shares'; expenses overstated by ₹26.34 crore across FY22 and FY23 for 'services not rendered', which SEBI treats as diversion of the company's funds. Dabkara must recover the diverted amount.

Penalties: company ₹12 lakh, Dabkara ₹28 lakh, Agarwal ₹19 lakh, Sharma ₹13 lakh, Sheikh ₹6 lakh, two independent directors ₹4 lakh each, the former compliance officer ₹2 lakh: ₹88 lakh in all, payable within 45 days.

Context (older than a week): EKI listed on the BSE SME platform in April 2021 at ₹100-102 and was one of 2021's biggest multibaggers on the carbon-credit boom (5paisa: '70x since IPO'); it later fell sharply as profits dropped and auditors flagged accounting practices (Carbon Pulse, 2023). Price levels stay out of the reel (SEBI price-data rule).
curiosity_gaps: The regulator found ₹197 crore of revenue booked early and ₹26 crore paid out for services never rendered. The fines on nine people add up to ₹88 lakh, less than half of one percent of the first number.
A stock that went up about 70 times on a story about cleaning the air. What was actually inside the books, while retail investors were buying?
